summary: The generated contract layer looks consistent: api/openapi.json and api/openapi-3.0.json carry the same 190 operationIds, each with an x-kudurru-permission extension written by internal/api/routes.go:42-88; the Go client, dashboard/src/api/generated.ts and docs-site/content/reference/api/endpoints.md cover them, and no file under internal/api changed after the last regeneration commit 1a78bb92. The runtime has two shapes: the "complete" SQLite runtime (cmd/kudurru/serve.go:1091-1175) and the Kubernetes legacy auth Stack (serve.go:1083-1090), plus role states on SQLite (static, enrolled follower, fenced/conflicted). Most 501/503 answers are intended and documented: static read_only (internal/api/static.go:28-33), SQLite-only RoleBinding/cluster/external-user/user commands (internal/api/rolebindings.go:88-91, cluster_enrollment.go:80-85, internal/auth/stack/routes.go:107-109,627-629, cmd/kudurru/serving_users_legacy.go:12-19), integrations on Kubernetes (internal/api/integrations.go:153-155, docs/deploy/integrations.md:11-17) and node-config 501 (internal/api/settings.go:505-506). Four refusal classes are not explained to the caller: (1) on Kubernetes six forwarded routes are not registered on the legacy mux and fall through to Go's plain-text 404 (internal/api/authcli.go:30-32, authroutes.go:106-107, rolebindings.go:107 versus internal/auth/stack/routes.go:77-105); (2) on an enrolled follower every non-forwarded mutation answers the generic 503 "current writable serving generation unavailable" (cmd/kudurru/serving_settings_api.go:109-112) and GET /cluster exposes no role (internal/api/nodes.go:55-64); (3) fenced/conflicted nodes answer 503 generation_pending with Retry-After 1s for a durable state (internal/servinghttp/http.go:150); (4) the vestigial gate in cmd/kudurru/serving_routes.go:16-63 still answers 503 current_command_unavailable for unregistered unsafe paths. Architecture pages do describe the D355-D366 flows (docs/architecture/configuration-and-store.md:1033-1085, 1238-1262, 1809-2137; access.md:1059-1069; zones.md:739-746, 887-927) but about a dozen "remains unfinished" statements now contradict the code. Operator docs still declare v0.1.0 (docs/guide/README.md:34, docs-site/content/_index.md:19) and have no page for RFC 2136, TOTP, session inventory or the Kubernetes grant-floor Secret. The permission lint is one-directional: about 18 declared verbs have no route, and GET /queries/export uses querylog.read although querylog.export exists (internal/api/query_export.go:26, internal/rbac/permissions.yaml:15,65). I found no G21 blocker that needs the owner.

remaining.title: Kubernetes: forwarded auth/IAM routes fall through to a plain-text 404
remaining.detail: On the Kubernetes driver the auth handler is a bare http.ServeMux holding only Stack routes plus two refusal sets (cmd/kudurru/serve.go:1085-1089). Six API routes are forwarded to it without a capability check and have no pattern there: GET /iam/rolebindings/{namespace}/{name} (internal/api/rolebindings.go:107), GET /auth/cli/providers, POST /auth/cli/{idp}/prepare, POST /auth/cli/{idp}/verify (internal/api/authcli.go:30-32), GET /auth/oidc/{idp}/logout and /logout/callback (internal/api/authroutes.go:106-107). The Stack route table is internal/auth/stack/routes.go:77-105. By static reading these answer Go's default text/plain '404 page not found', not the JSON envelope; `kudurru login` in its default OIDC mode and `kudurru iam rolebindings get` reach them. Fix: (1) serve GET rolebinding item from the Stack (a read, same data as the list); (2) register explicit envelope refusals for the CLI-login and logout-continuation routes in the style of registerUnavailableTOTP (cmd/kudurru/serving_totp_legacy.go:12-24) with a stable key and a hint, or implement provider advertisement on the Stack; (3) add a catch-all on the legacy mux that returns the envelope. Record the choice in the decision log. Confirm the 404 with a mounted envtest first; this finding is from reading only.
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:110 ('No unexplained 501/503 remains in supported workflows'); followup-audit.md:231 (F61a provider/client selection). Proof: envtest mounted test in cmd/kudurru (next to serve_tsig_kube_management_test.go) that requests each of the six routes on a Kubernetes runServe and asserts Content-Type application/json, an envelope key and a hint; CLI test that `kudurru login` against that server prints the refusal; TestOpenAPIDrift and TestRoutePermissionLint still pass.

remaining.title: Explicit role-aware refusals for followers, fenced and conflicted nodes, with a capability surface
remaining.detail: currentCommandAPIError maps replication.ErrReadOnly, ErrFenced and a dozen transient errors to one message, 503 unavailable 'current writable serving generation unavailable', with no hint (cmd/kudurru/serving_settings_api.go:109-112). An enrolled follower therefore answers that for PATCH /settings, /allowlist, /denylist, /domains, /queries/{id}/actions, unblock decisions, imports, IAM writes and TSIG commands; OIDC browser login answers 503 'captured browser provider login unavailable' (cmd/kudurru/serving_http_oidc.go:87). A fenced or conflicted node answers 503 generation_pending with Retry-After 1s (internal/servinghttp/http.go:150,156) although only `cluster resolve --offline` changes that state. GET /cluster has no role or authority field (internal/api/nodes.go:55-64) and the dashboard gates only static mode (dashboard/src/api/context.tsx:115-134). Work: distinct keys and hints (follower: names the primary and says the command is primary-only; fenced/conflict: names the offline commands and drops Retry-After); add role/authority to ClusterInfo; dashboard banner and disabled controls for non-forwarded domains; CLI prints the hint; regenerate OpenAPI and clients; update docs/deploy/sqlite-join.md and api-contracts.md.

recommendation:
Close G21 in this order. First G21-01 and G21-05: small, self-contained, and they remove the only responses that are plainly wrong (plain-text 404 on Kubernetes, 503 for unregistered paths, undeclared 501). Then G21-02, because explicit follower/fenced/conflict refusals are needed whatever is later forwarded: a partitioned or conflicted node will always refuse, and README.md:382 asks for that to be explicit. Then G21-11, so the allowlist becomes the maintained definition of "explained", and G21-13 as its documentation target. Run G21-12 last on the final SHA.

For the driver split, follow existing decisions instead of building parity: D54 keeps server-side session state on SQLite in v0.2, D364 lists per-session state on Kubernetes as a rejected alternative, D289 and D294 already ship SQLite-only administration with explicit refusals. Record one new decision that TOTP management, session inventory, external-account administration, API user commands and RoleBinding writes are SQLite-only in v0.2, each with a keyed refusal, a UI capability and a line in the matrix. That is an engineer decision, not an owner blocker.

For followers, follow D357/D362/D363: typed member commands that rerun the public route body on the primary, never a generic proxy (D362 rejects one). Forward the domains a dashboard behind a VIP uses (domain commands, unblock decisions, settings, own tokens and password); keep TSIG, imports, integrations and IAM administration primary-only with the G21-02 hint and one decision entry. For UPDATE on followers (G21-04) either choice is defensible; the tracker text prefers routing.

The surface items G21-08, -09 and -10 are real builds owned by G12, G09 and G11. They cannot be closed by documentation: followups.md:14-15 says requirements stay in scope unless the owner retargets them. The docs packages G21-14, -15 and -16 have no code dependency and can run in parallel now.

risks: This sweep is static. The Kubernetes plain-text 404 (G21-01), the follower message mapping and the SERVFAIL on follower UPDATE come from reading code paths, not from a run; confirm each with a mounted test before fixing.

Any route, description or status change regenerates five artifacts (two OpenAPI files, Go client and dispatch, dashboard generated.ts, endpoints.md, possibly cli.md). Parallel packages touching routes will conflict there; land route changes serially and regenerate once.
Decision-log numbering: several packages here add entries starting at D367; parallel work on other gates will collide in dev-docs/design-record.md and the three ledger files.

HEAD 33ee04bc has no hosted CI result in the ledger, and the hosted failure of TestRunServeDirectAnchorsBootstrapTransportsRestartAndDisabled is recorded as unexplained and open (completion-plan.md:1768-1775). G21 cannot be signed off on a red or unknown head.

G21 is worded as 'every feature'. V2-OBS items (dnstap, OTel/TRACEPARENT, ClickHouse/Loki) have no code under internal/, cmd/ or ee/ and no F row, only gaps.md:87; integrations on Kubernetes (F09b) and the IAM CRUD planned at design-record.md:1209 are also unbuilt. Dashboard changes must follow dashboard/AGENTS.md and the Astryx lookup rule in CLAUDE.md; the working tree has a modified dashboard/dist/index.html that must not be committed (release-checklist.md:103).
The docs retarget (G21-15) is large and editorial; statements about AD must stay 'preview' (D353) and two-VM VIP acceptance must stay 'deferred, not passed' (D358).
Making refusals explicit changes error keys that scripts may match on (for example 'unavailable' becoming a follower-specific key); note it in the changelog and keep HTTP status 503.

designOptions.name: A. Explicit refusals and documentation only
designOptions.description: Keep today's forwarding set and driver split. Add role-aware keys and hints, a role field on GET /cluster, UI capability gating, the capability matrix and the inventory test (G21-01, -02, -05, -11, -13).
designOptions.pros: Smallest change; needed in every option; closes the literal '501/503 explained' sentence; no new replication surface.
designOptions.cons: A dashboard reached through a VIP on a follower still cannot edit allowlists, approve requests, change settings or sign in with OIDC; the tracker lists that forwarding as remaining (completion-plan.md:1777-1778).

designOptions.name: B. Option A plus typed forwarding for dashboard-critical domains
designOptions.description: Add member commands for domain convenience commands, unblock decisions, settings PATCH and own tokens/password, following D357/D362/D363; record TSIG, imports, integrations and IAM administration as primary-only.
designOptions.pros: Makes the HA dashboard workflow usable on any member; reuses a proven pattern and its test harness; leaves a short, justified primary-only list.
designOptions.cons: Large; each domain needs its own reauthorization, dedup and rollback tests; depends on F60b/G11 work in the same files.

designOptions.name: C. Full parity
designOptions.description: Forward every mutation domain and OIDC login from followers, and build Kubernetes equivalents for TOTP, sessions, external accounts, user commands and RoleBinding writes.
designOptions.pros: No driver or role limits left to document.
designOptions.cons: Contradicts D54 and the alternative rejected in D364 (server-side session state on Kubernetes); very large; multi-object atomicity on Kubernetes would need a new design per feature as D365/D366 did.
